claim_boundary: These rows relate disclosure fields to source topics. They do not show conformity, certification, airworthiness approval, maintenance release, or regulatory filing.

sources.title: NPA 2025-07(B): proposed DS.AI
sources.status_note: Consultation closed 2026-03-10; not a final rule. Proposed DS.AI.010 scope is limited to specified high-risk Level 1 or 2 systems and excludes further cases; listing Level 3 in the classification table does not bring Level 3 into scope.

sources.title: AI Concept Paper Issue 2: Level 1 and 2 ML applications
sources.status_note: Concept paper, not an approval of any product.

sources.title: Roadmap for Artificial Intelligence Safety Assurance, Version I
sources.status_note: Guiding principles and plans, not an applicant-specific certification basis.

sources.title: WG-114 deliverables: ED-324
sources.status_note: ED-324 listed as draft; target publication 2026-12-31 as checked 2026-10-14.

sources.title: ARP4754B public product description
sources.status_note: Only the public description and standard identifier are referenced. No objective mapping has been verified from licensed text.

sources.title: DO-178C public standards overview
sources.status_note: Published in 2011; exact date not verified here. Only the public description and standard identifier are referenced. No objective mapping has been verified from licensed text.

sources.title: AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 Core
sources.status_note: NIST says AI RMF 1.0 is being revised. Its functions are not a certification checklist.

sources.title: Part-145, 145.A.50 certification of maintenance
sources.status_note: Consult current revision and organisation authorisations for an actual release to service.

sources.title: 14 CFR § 43.9 maintenance record entries
sources.status_note: Current eCFR checked 2026-10-14; U.S. maintenance-record scope only.

rows.title: Concept of operations
rows.applicability: A vendor describing the concept of operations and end-user role for a system within the proposal's DS.AI.010 scope.
rows.connection: The fields disclose intended use and the allocation of work between system and human.
rows.limit: A filled card does not demonstrate the proposal's objective or an accepted ConOps.

rows.title: AI level classification
rows.applicability: Vendor-declared AI level for a system being assessed against the proposal's DS.AI.010 scope.
rows.connection: Records the claimed level and the human authority posture for review.
rows.limit: The proposed DS.AI requirements are scoped to specified high-risk Level 1 and 2 systems, with further exclusions. Its table describes Level 3A and reserves Level 3B, but that does not make Level 3 systems in scope. A boolean alone cannot establish classification or human authority.

rows.title: Operational domain
rows.applicability: A system within the proposal's DS.AI.010 scope with defined operating conditions.
rows.connection: Declares operating limits and links each declared condition to evidence references.
rows.limit: Linked evidence is not verified by this crosswalk; declared-bin coverage is not real-world representativeness or approval.

rows.title: Risk and assurance allocation
rows.applicability: A system within the proposal's DS.AI.010 scope when an applicant has a documented safety assessment and allocated assurance level.
rows.connection: Captures a vendor's declared target and related standards posture for later review.
rows.limit: No DAL can be inferred from the AI level alone. The card cannot assign, verify, or approve a DAL.

rows.title: Learning assurance
rows.applicability: Learning-based aviation systems within the concept paper's Level 1 or 2 scope.
rows.connection: Points a reviewer to process and dataset evidence without copying restricted datasets into the card.
rows.limit: Concept-paper alignment is not an EASA approval or complete learning-assurance demonstration.

rows.title: FAA learning system
rows.reference_id: Guiding principles: learned versus learning AI; work within the aviation ecosystem
rows.applicability: FAA-oriented safety-assurance discussion for AI in aircraft and related systems.
rows.connection: Prompts explicit intended-use and learning-process documentation.
rows.limit: The roadmap sets research and policy direction, not a product-specific certification method.

rows.title: ED-324 status
rows.applicability: Only where the eventual ML process standard is relevant to the system and applicant.
rows.connection: A status field can disclose that the standard is being monitored or evaluated.
rows.limit: No published ED-324 objective or conformity claim is made. Target publication dates can move.

rows.title: ARP4754B applicability
rows.applicability: Aircraft and system development where the applicant identifies an applicable certification basis; not automatically MRO analytics.
rows.connection: Records an identifier-level standards posture and allocated system-level assurance target.
rows.limit: Licensed objective text and objective numbers are not reproduced or asserted.

rows.title: DO-178C applicability
rows.reference_id: DO-178C / ED-12C; objective ID not verified
rows.applicability: Airborne software when it forms part of the applicant's accepted assurance approach; not automatically off-aircraft maintenance tools.
rows.connection: Records that a vendor cites the standard identifier and can link its own evidence.
rows.limit: This row does not claim a particular DO-178C objective, software level, or compliance.

rows.title: NIST AI RMF context
rows.applicability: Voluntary risk-management context for organizations using or developing AI.
rows.connection: Makes purpose and operating context explicit for human review.
rows.limit: NIST AI RMF is voluntary and not an aviation approval checklist.

rows.title: NIST AI RMF measurement
rows.applicability: Voluntary choice of measurement methods for significant identified AI risks.
rows.connection: Points to bounded ODD evidence and leakage checks to be judged on their merits.
rows.limit: A reference or hash does not prove measurement quality, dataset rights, or representativeness.

rows.title: EU maintenance release separation
rows.applicability: EASA Part-145 maintenance where an appropriately authorised certifying staff member issues a separate release to service.
rows.connection: A review card can point to a human and the organisation's separate authorisation record.
rows.limit: A review-card signature does not verify staff privileges or issue a certificate of release to service.

rows.title: U.S. maintenance record separation
rows.applicability: U.S. maintenance records under this section; other inspection or operator programmes may have different rules.
rows.connection: An AI review card can travel as supporting evidence alongside the controlled maintenance record.
rows.limit: It does not replace the required work description, completion date, or qualifying signer's record.
